BUILD: a real billing and credits area for customers.

## Why
A user can see a balance and click "Top up". They cannot see where their credits went. The whole product positions against bill shock, and the ledger — which is append-only and auditable by design — is invisible to the person it is about.

## Read first
`lib/credits.ts` (the whole anti-bill-shock contract, `MICROS_PER_CREDIT`, `SIGNUP_GRANT`, `getBalance`, `spentInWindow`, `getSpendCapStatus`, `averageBuildCredits`, `estimateCredits`), `lib/stripe.ts` (`CREDIT_PACKS`, `billingEnabled()`), `app/dashboard/page.tsx`, `components/CreditMeter.tsx`, `app/dashboard/TopUpButton.tsx`, `app/settings/page.tsx`, and `app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx` — that last one already renders a ledger statement well, and the customer-facing version should be at least as clear.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT: `app/dashboard/billing/**`, `app/dashboard/TopUpButton.tsx`
Do NOT edit `app/dashboard/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/ProjectRow.tsx`, `app/settings/**`, `components/CreditMeter.tsx`, or anything under lib/ or app/api/. READ them.

## Build
1. **`app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`** — the customer's own credit statement. Every ledger entry: date, what it was for, signed amount, running balance. Decode `reason` into plain English — it carries `build`, `signup_grant`, `stripe:<session>`, and a `reward:<platform>:[pending:]<hash>` state machine (see `app/api/rewards/_lib.ts`). **Never show a raw hash to a customer.** Link a build charge to the project it belongs to. Paginated.
2. **Spend summary** — balance, spent in the last 30 days, and the user's own measured average per build (`averageBuildCredits`). If a spend cap is set, show progress against it.
3. **Honest cost information.** `estimateCredits()` exists and has ZERO callers. Its own comment says the two measurements so far (144 and 472 credits) are not a distribution. If you surface an estimate anywhere, present it as a wide range with that uncertainty stated — **do not present a precise-looking number**, and do not quote a single "typical build costs X" figure.
4. **`TopUpButton.tsx`** — it currently only appears when `billingEnabled()`. Make the billing page degrade honestly when Stripe is unconfigured: show the statement, and say top-ups are unavailable rather than rendering a button that 503s.

## Constraints
- **Read-only on money.** Do not write to `CreditLedger`, do not grant or deduct anything, do not create Stripe sessions beyond what `TopUpButton` already does.
- **Do not restate the no-charge-on-failure promise unless you verify it** in `app/api/generate/route.ts`. It is true — confirm it yourself before writing it down. Note that a run which fails, self-repairs, then succeeds IS charged once for the whole run including the repair; if you mention repairs, say that accurately.
- Match the dashboard's visual idiom exactly: `rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`, `text-sm`, `tabular-nums` on figures, monochrome.
- Preserve the accessibility bar: real labels, `focus-visible:` states, `<main>` landmark if you add a page shell, no horizontal scroll at 380px.
- **No new white text on the brand gradient** (fails contrast; known accepted issue).
- DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, anything under lib/, app/api/**, app/globals.css, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` AND `npx eslint app lib components` must BOTH be clean. Parallel agents are running — errors in files you did not touch are not yours.

## Report back
What you built, how you decoded each `reason` form, what you verified about the charging behaviour, how the page behaves with Stripe unconfigured, and any claim you chose not to make.

Welcome to the Next.js documentation!

## What is Next.js?

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.

It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.

Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.

## How to use the docs

The docs are organized into 3 sections:

- [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
- [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
- [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.

Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.

## App Router and Pages Router

Next.js has two different routers:

- **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
- **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.

At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.

### React version handling

The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:

- **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.

- **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.

This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.

## Pre-requisite knowledge

Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:

- HTML
- CSS
- JavaScript
- React

If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.

## Accessibility

For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.

## Join our Community

If you have questions about anything related to Next.js, you're always welcome to ask our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bUG2bvbtHy), [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/nextjs), and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/nextjs).

## What I built

**`app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`** (new) — a server component at `/dashboard/billing`, `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>`, `max-w-4xl px-6 py-10`, matching the dashboard's monochrome `rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10` / `text-sm` / `tabular-nums` idiom throughout. Five sections:

1. **Spend summary** — three tiles: credits left, used in the last 30 days, and the user's own `averageBuildCredits`.
2. **Spending cap** — when set, a `role="progressbar"` bar with `aria-valuenow/min/max` and a real `aria-label`, spent-of-cap, remaining, and an amber state plus honest wording when reached; when unset, one line pointing at Settings. Reuses `getSpendCapStatus`/`spentInWindow` so the number shown is the one the cap actually enforces.
3. **Add credits** — `<TopUpButton>` fed from the server's own `CREDIT_PACKS`, or the honest unavailable message.
4. **Credit statement** — paginated table (25/page, `?page=N`, clamped), newest-first with `[{createdAt:"desc"},{id:"desc"}]` so row 0 on page 1 is the row that defines the balance. Columns: When (UTC), What for, Change (signed, coloured), Balance (`balanceAfter` — the running balance). Build charges link to `/projects/<id>`. `<caption class="sr-only">`, `scope="col"` headers, `nav aria-label` + `rel="prev"/"next"` pager, "Showing X–Y of Z".
5. **What a build costs** — `estimateCredits()`'s first caller.

**`app/dashboard/billing/ledger.ts`** (new) — `describeReason`, deterministic UTC date/time formatters, signed-credit formatting.

**`app/dashboard/TopUpButton.tsx`** — added optional `enabled` (default `true`) and `packs` (default = the existing hardcoded list, so the dashboard's prop-less `<TopUpButton />` is unchanged); `focus-visible:` rings and `type="button"` on all three controls; removed a misleading `aria-expanded={false}` on a trigger that unmounts when opened.

## How each `reason` is decoded

| Stored | Shown |
|---|---|
| `build` | "Site build" + link to the project; if `buildId` went NULL (project deleted), "The site this was for has since been deleted." |
| `signup_grant` | "Welcome credits" / "Added free when you created your account" |
| `stripe:<session>` | "Credit purchase" / "Paid top-up" — session id dropped |
| `reward:<platform>:<hash>` | "Discord/Instagram/… reward" via `PLATFORM_LABELS` |
| `reward:<platform>:pending:<hash>` | "… reward — on hold" / "Recorded. The credits are added once the hold period is up." (the delta-0 row) |
| anything else | "Credits added" / "Credits used" / "Account note" by sign |

No raw hash, session id, or raw `reason` reaches the customer — including via `title`, which the admin page uses but this one deliberately omits. The unknown branch describes by direction of money rather than echoing the string.

## What I verified about charging (`app/api/generate/route.ts`)

- `chargeForBuild` is called **only** inside the `succeeded = true` branch. Every failure path (thrown error, abort, no output) writes `creditsCharged: 0` and touches no ledger row.
- `totals` accumulate across **both** attempts of the repair loop, then a single `costMicros`/`creditsFor`/`chargeForBuild` runs after the loop — so a run that fails, self-repairs, then succeeds is charged **once for the whole run including the repair**. The page says exactly that.
- A zero-cost success writes no ledger row at all. Hence the statement's footnote: a build reaches it only if it succeeded *and* had measured cost.
- "Credits don't expire" checked against `lib/retention.ts` — `CreditLedger` is in `NEVER_PRUNED` ("Retained permanently") and no expiry logic exists anywhere.

## With Stripe unconfigured

The page renders in full — tiles, cap, statement, cost info. The Add credits section renders `<TopUpButton enabled={false} />`, which returns plain text ("Top-ups aren't available right now — card payments aren't set up on this deployment. Your credits and everything on this page are unaffected."), never a button that would 503 against `/api/billing/checkout`.

## Claims I chose not to make

- **No "typical build costs X".** The estimate is two ranges (`estimateCredits`: 120–550 create, 60–300 edit) framed as "wide brackets, not predictions", with the two measurements (144 and 472) named as a threefold spread and explicitly called not enough to call a typical build.
- **No fake personal average.** `averageBuildCredits` silently falls back to the 400-credit constant with no history. I gate the tile on a `db.build.count` of succeeded-and-charged builds and show "—" instead — otherwise the page would present a global constant as "your average".
- **No credit-to-dollar conversion.** `lib/stripe.ts` says "$1 = 500 credits list price… packs get a modest discount at volume", but `CREDIT_PACKS` sells 500 credits for $9 — 9× the stated list rate, not a discount. **The comment and the price table contradict each other**; worth someone resolving, and until then I quote only the pack prices themselves.
- **Nothing about where the card is stored.** Only the verified part: `mode: "payment"`, a single charge, no subscription.

## One gap, out of scope

The page has **no entry point** — `app/dashboard/page.tsx` is read-only for me, and `CreditMeter`'s "Top up" link goes to `/pricing`. It needs one line in the dashboard header:

```tsx
<Link href="/dashboard/billing" className="text-sm text-black/60 hover:text-black dark:text-white/60 dark:hover:text-white">Billing</Link>
```

I considered adding it via `TopUpButton` (the only dashboard-rendered file in my scope) but rejected it: the dashboard header is a non-wrapping flex row that already exceeds 380px, and it renders `TopUpButton` only when `billingEnabled()`, so the link would vanish in exactly the degraded case the page is built to handle.

Read-only on money throughout: no `CreditLedger` writes, no grants or deductions, no Stripe sessions beyond `TopUpButton`'s existing call.
